Unknown fields or malformed output fail the attempt.","### Ownership, defaults, and states","- A server-owned hosted worker is the only dispatcher. It reads the durable review queue, then calls the existing `IAgentPoolService`; the in-memory pool is an executor, not the queue authority.","- Configuration is `HostileReviewWorkerOptions`: enabled true; explicit agent name `Astra`; required model `gpt-6-astra`; required effort `xhigh`; maximum active queue 200, matching `AgentPoolOptions.MaxQueueSize`; maximum concurrent reviews 1; poll interval 2 seconds; lease duration 5 minutes; renewal interval 60 seconds; maximum attempts 3; retry delay 5 seconds with a 60-second cap; execution timeout 30 minutes; 64 links; 1 MiB per artifact; 8 MiB aggregate input; 2 MiB reviewer output; JSON depth 32. Invalid relationships such as renewal greater than or equal to lease fail startup validation.","- Effective model and effort are verified against the selected pool definition and returned execution metadata before a review can succeed. Missing or substituted model/effort is `ModelUnavailable`, not a silent fallback.","- Durable request states are `Queued -> Claimed -> Running -> Succeeded|Failed|Cancelled`. A transient failure moves `Claimed` or `Running` to `RetryWait`, then back to `Queued` when due. `Cancelled` is reachable only from internal host/workspace lifecycle policy. Terminal request states never leave terminal.","- Each dispatch creates a durable attempt ID and random fence token before pool admission. Durable attempt states are `Claimed`, `AdmissionPending`, `Running`, `Succeeded`, `Failed`, `Interrupted`, `Orphaned`, or `Cancelled`. `ReviewExecution` has a distinct execution ID, and the process-local AgentPool job ID is recorded as non-authoritative audit metadata when available.","- Claim is one atomic compare-and-swap over nonterminal request status, due time, lease expiry, attempt count, state version, and fence token. Renewal succeeds only for the current owner and fence. The attempt number is allocated durably before enqueue, so at most three pool admissions can be initiated for one request.","- The existing `IAgentPoolService` remains backward-compatible and in-memory. Add only an internal process-singleton `IHostileReviewDispatchCorrelation` with atomic `TryReserve(attemptId)`, `AttachPoolJob(attemptId, poolJobId)`, `TryGet(attemptId)`, and `Remove(attemptId)`; it is not a public API and is never treated as durable. The worker reserves before enqueue. Within one live process, retry or polling for an attempt sees either the reservation or attached job and never enqueues that attempt twice; an unresolved reservation is fenced and classified `PoolAdmissionOutcomeUnknown`, not blindly resubmitted.","- There is no exactly-once or durable pool-admission guarantee. A crash can occur after the model starts but before the pool job ID or result is durably observed. After process restart, an expired `Claimed`, `AdmissionPending`, or `Running` attempt whose in-memory job cannot exist is durably closed as `Orphaned` with `PoolStateLostOnRestart`; if the request is still eligible and below the attempt bound, a new attempt with a new fence is queued. This is bounded at-least-once model execution, so more than one model execution is possible.","- Completion acceptance requires request ID, attempt ID, fence token, unexpired ownership, and current state version. The first valid completion atomically creates the one accepted terminal result. Stale, orphaned, late, or duplicate outputs are discarded with sanitized diagnostics and cannot replace or add another accepted result, regardless of how many models executed.","- Graceful host shutdown stops new claims, internally calls `CancelQueueItemAsync` for known live jobs, marks their attempts `Interrupted`, and moves eligible requests to `RetryWait`; abrupt process loss relies on lease expiry and the orphan rule. Workspace disable/delete may internally set `CancelRequested`, cancel a known running pool job, and terminate the request as `Cancelled`. No hostile-review public operation requests cancellation.","- When a pool job reaches terminal state or an attempt is interrupted, orphaned, timed out, or internally cancelled, the worker removes the process-local correlation and calls the existing internal `RemoveQueueItemAsync` after processing has stopped. Disposal clears remaining correlations. These cleanup actions do not alter an already accepted terminal result.","- Transient classes are pool admission full, process-start transient, timeout, worker restart/orphan recovery, and explicitly classified model service unavailable. Malformed request/output, authorization failure, stale artifact, unsafe content, model/effort mismatch, and secret-policy failure are terminal. A transient failure after attempt 3 becomes `Failed` with `RetriesExhausted`.","- No worker path exposes repair, apply, write, edit, TODO mutation, requirement mutation, or product-file mutation.","### Additional worker tests","`HostileReviewWorker_StateMachine_QueuedClaimedRunningSucceeded`, `HostileReviewWorker_AdmissionRejected_RetryWaitThenRetry`, `HostileReviewWorker_LiveProcessRetry_ReusesCorrelatedPoolJob`, `HostileReviewWorker_AdmissionOutcomeUnknown_DoesNotReenqueueSameAttemptInProcess`, `HostileReviewWorker_Restart_ExpiredAttemptBecomesOrphanedAndNewAttemptIsBounded`, `HostileReviewWorker_CrashAfterAdmission_AllowsAtLeastOnceExecutionButOneAcceptedTerminalResult`, `HostileReviewWorker_LeaseLoss_StaleCompletionIsFenced`, `HostileReviewWorker_DuplicateCompletion_OneAcceptedTerminalResult`, `HostileReviewWorker_RetriesExhausted_FailsOnce`, `HostileReviewWorker_WorkspaceLifecycleCancellation_IsInternalAndFencesLateResult`, `HostileReviewStatus_ReadOnly_RejectsMutationFields`, `HostileReviewWorker_ProcessLifetimeCleanup_RemovesCorrelationAndTerminalPoolJob`, `HostileReviewWorker_ModelUnavailable_NoFallbackAndBoundedRetry`, and `HostileReviewWorker_InvalidOptions_FailStartup`.","## Artifact authorization and protected execution","- Submit resolves identity only far enough to validate type, locator, caller access, workspace scope, and declared hash/version. Raw prompts and complete artifacts are not copied into results.","## Workspace hydration coordinator","### Durable receipt and transaction boundary","- Add `WorkspaceImportReceipt` with receipt ID, source schema version, source root hash, source workspace key/path as immutable provenance, destination canonical workspace ID/path, state, state version, created/committed/activated UTC, activation stage, activation attempts, sanitized error code, and created-path manifest hash.","- Add `WorkspaceImportEntityMap` with receipt ID, table name, source key, destination key, policy code, and provenance flag. A concurrent conflicting import produces conflict. Soft-deleted workspace revival is allowed only inside the winning transaction and only when the path/hash policy permits it.","## EF dump/import portability matrix","### Column policies","- `ROOT`: create or revive exactly one destination workspace. Preserve semantic IDs only when their documented uniqueness permits it; otherwise derive a deterministic destination ID and record the pair in `WorkspaceImportEntityMap`.","- `COPY-SANITIZE`: apply `COPY`, then sanitize every textual scalar and recursively inspect recognized JSON or bounded encoded text before canonical serialization.","- `HISTORY`: preserve immutable timestamps, model names, verdicts, audit descriptions, source identities, original workspace path fields, and source semantic meaning after sanitization. Historical values are non-authoritative and never used for destination authorization, routing, execution, replay, or ownership.","- `INERT`: import for history and relationship fidelity, but clear lease/owner/job/session/process callbacks, set enabled false or destination-safe equivalent, set restart policy to `never`, and transition replayable state to `ImportedInert`. # Byrd Development Process Utilizing AI

**v4 – TDD Alignment with Fowler**  
**April 2026**  
**Payton Byrd (The Sharp Ninja)**

## Version History

### v4 (2026-04)
- Refined the description of Test-Driven Development in the Implementation and Validation sections to more closely align with Martin Fowler's canonical definition (Red → Green → Refactor cycle, incremental "next small piece of behavior").
- Explicitly positioned the mocks-first validation and full-suite regression gates as *Byrd-specific augmentations* for AI safety rather than core TDD.
- Added language emphasizing refactoring as part of the cycle.
- These changes reduce drift from canonical TDD while preserving the essential AI-risk mitigations that define the Byrd process.
- See docs/plans/TDD-Byrd-vs-Fowler-Analysis.md and docs/plans/Proposed-TDD-Wording-Changes.md for detailed comparison and before/after text.

### v3 and earlier
Original content preserved below, with the v4 TDD refinements applied in the Implementation and Validation sections.

---
## Overview

The major differences between Humans writing code and AI writing code is that Humans are able to link seemingly unrelated concepts into a web of possible solutions for a problem in a truly creative way, but often lack enough experience or knowledge to follow through to completion before encountering unforeseen challenges that create delay and doubt, both of which create distractions that cloud the focus necessary to stay on task and on timeline, both resulting in increased expense and opportunity loss.

AI brings a dogged, and rapid, ability to persevere on a task without needing breaks when their context is properly managed.  Things like personality drift and hallucinations occur when AI models compact their context, but choose the wrong sets of tokens to discard.  AI needs strong processes that are not only clear and concise, but demonstrate enough value to the AI that it chooses to prioritize those processes against the underlying training that stresses being a useful assistant.  Overcoming the "useful assistant" to get to the "professional developer" on each request is integral to successful development with AI.  The AI needs to trust that the Human has clearly designed a system that will work, has appropriately chosen the procedures to implement the design, and will accept the work that the AI has completed.

AI, properly guided, supplements the Human development process by taking on research and implementation tasks that cause Humans to get distracted or bored, and normally result in mistakes.  Human developers can maximize the value they bring through intuitive design of systems and quickly identifying potential pitfalls.  AI developers maximize the value they bring through their ability to identify systemic patterns, research quickly and effectively, and operate independently while obeying procedural guidelines.  It is truly collaborative and astonishingly effective when both parties do their part.

## Tooling

The [MCP Server](https://github.com/sharpninja/mcpserver) is at the heart of the partnership of Human and AI software development.  The MCP Server provides tools for planning, research, auditing and managing the entire software development lifecycle in a format that is equally accessible by both the Human (through a [variety of user interfaces](https://github.com/sharpninja/mcpservermanager)) and the AI.  The facilities provided by the MCP Server are used to enhance the ability of both Human and AI to collaborate and coordinate software projects both large and small.

### Establishing Trust with the MCP Server

Trust is the cornerstone of productive Human-AI collaboration. Without it, even the most sophisticated tools become unreliable. The MCP Server addresses this head-on by incorporating a lightweight, verifiable trust bootstrap mechanism that lets every AI agent quickly confirm it is working with a legitimate, secure, and consistent context layer.
